subtitle: Sarojini Naidu and the Salt that Stung an Empire

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of Sarojini Naidu at the head of a silent column of satyagrahis, distant salt pans glimmering in harsh sun, armed policemen faint on the horizon
panels.action: Sarojini Naidu stands calm yet unyielding at the front of an unarmed procession near the Dharasana Salt Works, her white sari and determined gaze set against the shimmering salt fields and an approaching line of baton-armed police.

dialogue.text: May 1930: with Gandhi in prison, it is Sarojini Naidu who walks unarmed towards Dharasana, where lathis, salt, and the world’s press will collide.

i18n.hi: मई 1930: गांधी जेल में हैं, तो बिना हथियार सरोजिनी नायडू ही धारासना की ओर बढ़ती हैं, जहाँ लाठी, नमक और दुनिया की नज़रें टकराएँगी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Sarojini Naidu seated by lamplight, reading a telegram, shadows long on the mud floor
panels.action: In a dim ashram room, Sarojini Naidu sits cross-legged by a flickering lamp, holding a telegram about Gandhi’s arrest, her face tightening with resolve as the light catches the lines of fatigue and fire.

dialogue.text: On the night of 4 May 1930, news moves faster than the trains: Gandhi has been arrested on the march to the sea. The salt satyagraha leader is gone.

i18n.hi: 4 मई 1930 की रात, खबर रेल से तेज दौड़ती है: गांधी समुद्र की ओर मार्च करते हुए गिरफ़्तार हो गए। नमक सत्याग्रह का नेता उठा लिया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot, profile, Sarojini rising, others’ silhouettes in the doorway behind her
panels.action: Sarojini Naidu rises from the floor, sari rustling, as shadowy figures of volunteers gather at the door, eyes fixed on her for direction.

dialogue.speaker: sarojini_naidu
dialogue.text: They have taken Bapu. The road to Dharasana is now ours.

i18n.hi: बापू को ले गए। अब धारासना की राह हमारी है।

panels.shot: wide shot of an improvised meeting under a tree, Sarojini addressing men and women seated on the ground
panels.action: Under a spreading banyan tree, Sarojini stands on a low platform, addressing a crowd of men in khadi caps and women in plain saris, all listening in tense silence.

dialogue.text: Abbas Tyabji, the old judge turned rebel, is arrested next. The British hope Dharasana will fall silent. Instead, the Congress turns to the Nightingale of India.

i18n.hi: फिर अब्बास तैयबजी, बुज़ुर्ग जज से बने बाग़ी, गिरफ़्तार होते हैं। अंग्रेज़ सोचते हैं धारासना चुप हो जाएगा। पर कांग्रेस मुड़ती है भारत की बुलबुल की ओर।

panels.shot: close-up on Sarojini’s face as she speaks, eyes steady, a notebook with Gandhi’s instructions visible in her hand
panels.action: Sarojini holds a small notebook in one hand, thumb resting on a page, as she addresses the volunteers, her eyes firm under arched brows.

dialogue.speaker: sarojini_naidu
dialogue.text: You will not raise a hand in anger. Your courage will be your only shield.

i18n.hi: गुस्से में हाथ मत उठाना। तुम्हारी ढाल बस तुम्हारा साहस होगा।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of training: rows of satyagrahis sitting, then standing, hands folded, as a few practice taking mock blows without flinching
panels.action: In an open compound, volunteers in simple khadi practice walking in pairs and kneeling, a few bracing themselves as comrades lightly tap their shoulders with sticks, learning to stand firm.

dialogue.text: For days, they drill not in swordplay but in stillness. To move towards violence and not answer it is a different kind of training.

i18n.hi: कई दिन तक अभ्यास तलवार का नहीं, ठहराव का होता है। हिंसा की ओर बढ़कर जवाब न देना एक अलग तरह की साधना है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a smaller circle of women around Sarojini; one young woman speaks, anxious
panels.action: A cluster of women sit close around Sarojini, one younger woman leaning forward, brows knit, as Sarojini listens, hand resting lightly on the woman’s arm.

dialogue.text: Women have already marched in cities, sold salt, courted arrest. Now, at Dharasana, they will be in the very front ranks.

i18n.hi: औरतें शहर–शहर मार्च कर चुकी हैं, नमक बेच चुकी हैं, जेल झेल चुकी हैं। अब धारासना में वे सबसे आगे की कतार में होंगी।

panels.shot: pre-dawn wide shot: long line of satyagrahis on a dusty road, silhouettes against first light, Sarojini at the head
panels.action: Before sunrise, a long, silent column moves along a dusty Gujarati road; Sarojini walks at the head, palms joined, the horizon just beginning to glow.

dialogue.text: On 21 May, they set out for the Dharasana Salt Works. No weapons, no helmets, only cotton cloth and a decision.

i18n.hi: 21 मई को वे धारासना साल्ट वर्क्स की ओर निकल पड़ते हैं। न हथियार, न हेलमेट, बस सूती कपड़े और एक ठान ली हुई बात।

panels.shot: low wide shot from behind the satyagrahis as they approach the barbed-wire fence and a line of police with lathis
panels.action: The satyagrahis advance towards a barbed-wire fence guarding long rows of salt pans, where uniformed policemen stand shoulder to shoulder, steel-tipped lathis held across their chests.

dialogue.text: Ahead lies the white crust of government salt and a ring of armed police. The British state will defend its monopoly with seasoned lathis.

i18n.hi: आगे सरकार के नमक की सफेद परत है और सशस्त्र पुलिस की घेराबंदी। अंग्रेज़ी हुकूमत अपने नमक के एकाधिकार की रखवाली मँजे हुए डंडों से करेगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sarojini and a British police officer facing each other across a few feet of dust
panels.action: Sarojini stands a few strides from the fence, facing a British officer with a stiff cap and set jaw, as Indian constables wait behind him, gripping their batons.

dialogue.speaker: sarojini_naidu
dialogue.text: We come only to take salt that the sea gives freely.

i18n.hi: हम तो बस वही नमक लेने आए हैं जो समुंदर मुफ़्त देता है।

panels.shot: close-up on Sarojini’s hand raised slightly, signalling the first batch forward, police line tense in the background
panels.action: Sarojini lifts her hand in a small, deliberate gesture, signalling the first group of satyagrahis to step forward as the police line tenses.

dialogue.text: They approach in batches, kneeling at the fence. Each knows he may not stand up unaided.

i18n.hi: वे दलों में बढ़ते हैं, घुटनों के बल बाड़ तक झुकते हैं। हर एक जानता है कि शायद उठ नहीं पाएगा।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot capturing the arc of a raised lathi and the calm, bowed head of the first satyagraha volunteer
panels.action: A policeman’s lathi swings in a hard arc towards the shoulders of a kneeling volunteer, whose head is bowed and hands rest calmly on his thighs.

dialogue.text: Then the lathis fall. Webb Miller will write of steel-tipped clubs smashing into unprotected shoulders and backs, again and again.

i18n.hi: फिर लाठियाँ बरसती हैं। वेब मिलर लिखेगा कैसे लोहे जड़ी डंडियाँ निहत्थे कंधों और पीठों पर बार–बार टूटती रहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sarojini turned slightly away, eyes tightened but body steady as more blows fall in the background
panels.action: Sarojini stands with jaw clenched, eyes shining but dry, as behind her more satyagrahis kneel and receive blow after blow from the police.

dialogue.speaker: sarojini_naidu
dialogue.text: Remember, no cry for mercy. Let the world be our witness.

i18n.hi: याद रखो, दया की गुहार नहीं। दुनिया को हमारा गवाह बनने दो।

panels.shot: wide shot of the ground: rows of prone satyagrahis being carried away by comrades while another batch walks forward
panels.action: On the dusty ground, rows of volunteers lie still as comrades gently lift and carry them away, while another batch rises from the rear and walks forward to take their place.

dialogue.text: As each line crumples, another steps in. Miller counts men dropping in tens and dozens, some unconscious, some barely able to crawl.

i18n.hi: हर कतार गिरती है तो अगली आ खड़ी होती है। मिलर दर्ज करता है कि कैसे लोग दस–दस, दर्जनों की तादाद में ढेर हो रहे हैं, कोई बेहोश, कोई रेंग भर पा रहा है।

panels.shot: close-up on a satyagrahi’s face as he grimaces, teeth clenched, yet does not raise an arm to defend himself
panels.action: A kneeling satyagrahi’s face tightens in pain, eyes squeezed shut, as a lathi descends just outside the frame; his hands remain at his sides.

dialogue.text: He notes too that not one strike is returned. No stone flies, no fist is raised. This, he cables, is 'one of the most brutal and cold-blooded' scenes he has seen.

i18n.hi: वह यह भी नोट करता है कि एक भी चोट का जवाब नहीं आता। न कोई पत्थर उड़ता है, न मुट्ठी उठती है। यह, वह तार से भेजता है, ‘उसके देखे हुए सबसे निर्मम, बेहिस लहज़ों’ में से एक है।

panels.shot: interior newsroom wide shot: editors crowded around a teleprinter as a clerk types, a strip of paper bearing Miller’s dispatch curling out
panels.action: In a foreign newsroom cluttered with papers and maps, editors lean over a teleprinter as a clerk types, the long strip of Miller’s Dharasana dispatch curling out onto the desk.

dialogue.text: British officials try to stop the story, but United Press cables it out. In America, in Europe, readers learn of unarmed Indians beaten at a salt depot.

i18n.hi: ब्रिटिश अफ़सर ख़बर रोकने की कोशिश करते हैं, पर यूनाइटेड प्रेस इसे दुनिया भर में भेज देता है। अमरीका और यूरोप में लोग पढ़ते हैं कि कैसे निहत्थे भारतीयों को एक नमकगोदाम पर पीटा गया।

panels.shot: formal wide shot of the United States Senate chamber, a senator standing, reading from a sheet as others listen
panels.action: In the high-ceilinged United States Senate chamber, a senator stands with a paper in hand, reading aloud as other senators sit listening on leather benches.

dialogue.text: In May 1930, Miller’s words are read into the United States Congressional Record. Dharasana enters the debates of another parliament, half a world away.

i18n.hi: मई 1930 में, मिलर की रिपोर्ट अमरीकी संसद के रिकॉर्ड में पढ़ी जाती है। धारासना आधी दुनिया दूर दूसरी संसद की बहसों में दर्ज हो जाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot: back in camp, Sarojini sitting among injured volunteers, bandaged heads and shoulders around her
panels.action: Later, in a makeshift camp, Sarojini sits on a cot among volunteers with bandaged heads and shoulders, her hand resting gently on the arm of a man lying beside her.

dialogue.text: Civil disobedience does not topple the Raj in a day. But historians will point to Dharasana as the moment when non-violence and modern communication fused into a new kind of power.

i18n.hi: सविनय अवज्ञा एक दिन में राज नहीं गिराती। पर इतिहासकार धारासना को वह घड़ी कहेंगे जब अहिंसा और आधुनिक संचार मिलकर एक नई ताकत बने।

panels.shot: close-up on Sarojini looking out of frame, distant salt pans and a hazy horizon reflected in her eyes
panels.action: Sarojini gazes towards the distant salt works, the white of the pans glinting faintly on the horizon, her expression a mix of weariness and unbroken resolve.

dialogue.text: At Dharasana, a poet and politician turned suffering into witness. Her name reminds us that leadership can wear a sari, and that courage can echo louder than any blow.

i18n.hi: धारासना में एक कवयित्री और राजनीतिज्ञ ने पीड़ा को गवाही में बदल दिया। उसका नाम याद दिलाता है कि नेतृत्व साड़ी भी पहन सकता है, और साहस किसी भी वार से ज़्यादा गूँज सकता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Sarojini Naidu and the Salt that Stung an Empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: सरोजिनी नायडू और नमक, जिसने साम्राज्य को जला दिया
